meta_description: Where to stay in Budapest: District V, VI, VII, VIII, the Castle District and Margaret Island compared, with 2 well-rated hotels in each from €79 a night.
h1: Where to Stay in Budapest (2026): Best Areas and Hotels
h1_main: Where to Stay in Budapest: 6 Best Areas
author_role: 6 areas compared on walking distance, metro, atmosphere and hotel prices, with 2 well-rated hotels in each
lead: The right area to stay in Budapest is the one that fits your trip: District V downtown if it is your first visit and you want to walk everywhere (start with Prestige Hotel by the Chain Bridge), District VI around the Opera and Andrássy Avenue for grand boulevards, District VII for ruin bars and the Jewish Quarter, or the Castle District for quiet cobbled lanes. Staying near a spa instead? See the spa hotels. This page gets you to the right area, and a hotel in it, in under a minute.

To make the choice easy, I compared 6 areas on what decides where you sleep: how far you walk to the Basilica, Parliament and the river, the nearest metro, the atmosphere at night, and what a well-rated hotel costs there on the same night, with 2 hotels per area checked on each hotel's own listing. Filter by area below, or scroll straight to the hotels.

guide.h2: Budapest's Best Areas Side by Side
guide.html:
Hotel prices are for the same night (Wednesday 10 March 2027, 2 adults, 1 room) at the two hotels we picked in each area.

AreaBest forFeels likeWalk to the sightsOur 2 hotels

District VI (Terézváros)Opera, Andrássy Avenue, families wanting suitesElegant boulevards, cafésOpera and House of Terror on foot; Liberty Square 1,800 ft from Mera€87–103
District VII (Jewish Quarter)Nightlife, food, synagoguesLively, late nightsDohány Synagogue and ruin bars on foot€89–120
District I (Castle District)Couples, history, quiet nightsCobbled, calmFisherman's Bastion, Matthias Church on foot; Pest across the river€79–153
District VIII (Palace Quarter, Corvin)Value, museumsResidential, localNational Museum and Central Market Hall on foot€64–79
District XIII and Margaret IslandSpa stays, quiet, greenCalm, riversideParliament 1 mi; old town by tram or bus€111–123

What the numbers say: the central areas are cheaper than most visitors expect. A 9.3-rated hotel in District VI (Mera) costs €87, and District VIII's picks are €64–79. You only pay a premium for the river and Chain Bridge in District V or for the castle address of the Hilton.

• First visit, 2–3 nights: District V. Prestige by the Chain Bridge or Danubius District V by Liberty Square.
  • Opera, cafés and Andrássy Avenue: District VI. Mera or the suites at Mamaison Izabella.
  • Nightlife and food: District VII. Roombach or Queen's Court.
  • Romantic and quiet: the Castle District. Hilton by Fisherman's Bastion or Castle Garden.
  • Best value: District VIII. Bo18 or Central Hotel 21.
  • Spa or a quiet stay: District XIII and Margaret Island.

Still deciding on the hotel itself? Compare the best hotels, boutique hotels, luxury hotels or cheap hotels.

Metro: District V and VI sit on the M1, M2 and M3 lines (Deák Ferenc tér, Opera, Arany János utca). District VII uses Astoria and Blaha Lujza tér (M2), District VIII Corvin-negyed and Rákóczi tér. The Castle District and Margaret Island have no metro; you get there by bus.

From the airport: see Budapest airport to the city centre, or stay the first night at an airport hotel.

Plan the days: our 3-day Budapest itinerary and the best things to do in Budapest show which sights cluster in each area.

faqs.q: What is the best area to stay in Budapest?
faqs.a: For a first visit, District V (Belváros and Lipótváros) on the Pest side: the Basilica, Parliament, the Chain Bridge and Váci utca are all walkable.

faqs.q: Is it better to stay in Buda or Pest?
faqs.a: Pest for most visitors: it has the main sights, restaurants and metro lines. Buda's Castle District suits couples who want quiet, historic streets and do not mind buses.

faqs.q: Where should I stay in Budapest for nightlife?
faqs.a: District VII, the Jewish Quarter, where the ruin bars are. Roombach is 1,200 ft from the Dohány Street Synagogue; Queen's Court has a spa to recover in.

faqs.q: What is the cheapest good area to stay in Budapest?
faqs.a: District VIII. Bo18 (9.2) costs €79 and Central Hotel 21 (8.8) €64 for two on a March weeknight, both within walking distance of the National Museum.

faqs.q: Where to stay in Budapest with kids?
faqs.a: District VI's suite hotels, like Mamaison Residence Izabella with full kitchens and a children's breakfast discount, or Margaret Island for green space and pools.

methodology: We compared six areas on walking distance to the main sights, metro access and atmosphere, then picked two hotels in each that score at least 8.8 on hundreds or thousands of reviews, comparing their price for the same night (10 March 2027, 2 adults), location score and facilities on each hotel's live listing.
